methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia is a Series C–stage transportation company founded by Valery Miftakhov that has raised $380M+ to date. The comparable universe in Transportation is sparse: seven private companies populate the sector (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and Harbinger), with no public peers available for direct benchmarking.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method given data constraints. Stage-Progression triangulation applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $380M total raised proxy, yielding an implied value of $646M. The Peer-Median approach is inapplicable because no same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables within Transportation meet the threshold for statistical confidence (fewer than three datapoints in each filter).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $549M (low) to $743M (high), anchored to a median of $646M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodological input rather than triangulation across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties center on the absence of narrow peer multiples—the broader Transportation sector lacks sufficient public benchmarks and same-stage private valuations—and the use of historical capital raised as a proxy for current valuation, which may not capture recent operational milestones or market conditions. Additional financial and operational data would be required to strengthen conviction in this range.
